title: Reduce Docker image layer churn and deploy a remote build cache proxy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Our monorepo CI suffers from long cold-container pulls and frequent cache misses caused by non-deterministic Docker image layers (language runtimes, apt-installed packages, and varying build args). This increases developer iteration times and monthly CI spend. Goal: introduce a canonical minimal builder image family, standardize layer ordering and package pinning, and deploy a remote content-addressable cache proxy (S3-backed + authenticated proxy) so layer and build artifact reuse improves across ephemeral runners and dedicated agents. Success metrics: 1) 40% reduction in average job wall-clock time for unit/integration jobs that build artifacts; 2) 60% reduction in Docker pull bytes per pipeline run; 3) cache hit rate >= 75% for deterministic build steps; 4) first-merge to green time improved by 30% on average for dependent repos. Out of scope: changing language versions or switching primary tooling (we'll keep buildkite + remote executors). Plan (phased): Phase 0 - Discovery (complete): run image layer provenance audit across top 100 pipelines, identify top 12 sources of churn. Phase 1 - Image standardization (in progress): produce two canonical base images (builder-minimal: ubuntu:24.04-slim + pinned apt lists; runtime-ci: distroless language runtime image). Add automated base-image builder pipeline that produces SBOM and deterministic tags. Phase 2 - Remote cache proxy (starting 2025-02-20): deploy a CAS proxy service that fronts S3 cache and authenticates via CI tokens; integrate with BuildKit remote cache export/import for docker build and with our Bazel-like artifact upload path (where applicable). Phase 3 - Linter/toolchain alignment: replace ad-hoc linter containers with a single polylint shim image and add version-locking in repo-level config. Phase 4 - Rollout & telemetry: migrate 25% of pipelines to canonical images + remote cache, run for two weeks, evaluate metrics, then ramp. Acceptance criteria: canonical images build deterministically in CI (byte-for-byte reproducible layers between runs), remote cache hit rate > 50% in canary, no regression in existing job artifacts, documented migration guide and one internal workshop completed. Risks & mitigations: risk - some repos have implicit env assumptions -> mitigation: create a repo-level compatibility checklist and a migration harness that runs a compatibility smoke-test. risk - credentials leakage from remote cache -> mitigation: token-scoped access, short-lived CI tokens, and audit logs. Rollback plan: if regressions found during canary, switch affected pipelines back to pinned previous image tags and disable cache export. Artifacts & links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CI+Cache+and+Image+Standardization; RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/214; proto-implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls?q=remote-cache+ENG-40122; Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-cache/ci-cache-overview (canary panel). Notes for reviewers: prioritize deterministic packaging and minimal surface area changes to repo-level build scripts. Use incremental rollout with telemetry gating.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Discovery results: top churn causes are python pip cache invalidation (different cache keys), apt lists changing order, and ephemeral builder user IDs. Added recommended fixes to discovery doc.
2025-01-25 - Design review with Infra and Platform: agreed on two canonical images, use BuildKit v0.12+ with inline cache export/import and s3-backed registry proxy.
2025-02-02 - Security reviewed: token scoping and KMS rotation accepted; will add audit log dashboard before phase 2 rollout.
2025-02-18 - Implementation update: builder-minimal image recipe landed in infra repo (PR #7683). Early smoke runs passed for 8/12 high-volume pipelines.
2025-02-26 - Canary started: 25% pipelines using remote cache proxy; initial cache hit rate ~62%, average job time reduced 28% for canary group. Collecting more samples.
2025-02-28 - PM feedback from Lina Ortega: ensure migration docs include example of pinning third-party apt sources and pip constraints.txt best practices. Added to checklist.
